decisions.title: Who invited that baby?
decisions.situation: There is a baby in the mirror. They copy every move you make. You have concerns about their manners.

result.title: Extremely rude guest
result.body: They pull it right back. You laugh and try another one.

journal.text: I made faces at my reflection and laughed when it copied me.

decisions.title: Permanent exhibition
decisions.situation: You draw a huge purple person on the wall. Alice walks in while you are adding the teeth.

result.title: Mixed reviews
result.body: Alice gives you paper. The wall gets a long scrub.

journal.text: I drew a purple person on the wall. It was not a commissioned piece.

decisions.title: Something in your sock
decisions.situation: You hide an ice cube in your sock. Alice asks why your foot is leaking. You had not planned for questions.

choices.label: Ask to put your sock in the freezer

result.title: One wet sock
result.body: You turn the sock out over a bowl. A tiny cube slides out. Alice supplies a dry sock; you inspect the bowl for the rest of your treasure.

journal.text: I showed Alice the ice cube I had hidden in my sock.

decisions.title: Customer complaint
decisions.situation: Alice takes you for a haircut. You are convinced the cape means you have been promoted to wizard.

choices.label: Cast a spell on the comb
Ask Alice to hold your hand

result.title: Comb survives
result.body: The comb refuses to turn into a frog. Your haircut carries on.

journal.text: I tried magic during a haircut. It did not affect the comb.

decisions.title: The museum has escaped
decisions.situation: You empty your pocket collection onto the table for Alice. Three stones. A leaf. A slug you thought was another leaf. The slug makes for the edge.

choices.label: Return the slug before it reaches the floor
Claim the slug lives here now

result.title: Please follow the shiny line
result.body: You describe the stones while Alice catches the slug on a leaf. Your only moving exhibit is removed halfway through the tour.

journal.text: I gave Alice a museum tour while a slug escaped from my pocket collection.

decisions.title: They do not find it funny
decisions.situation: Someone keeps making a joke out of Lorenzo’s name. Lorenzo has stopped correcting them.

choices.label: Use their name properly and speak up

result.title: A little backup
result.body: You say it is getting old. Lorenzo thanks you later.

journal.text: I backed Lorenzo when someone kept mocking their name.

decisions.title: A disappointing lunch
decisions.situation: Lorenzo opens a lunchbox with nothing in it. They look embarrassed. Leonardo is nearby.

result.title: Lunch gets sorted
result.body: Leonardo helps without making an announcement. Lorenzo looks relieved.

journal.text: I quietly got Leonardo’s help when Lorenzo had no lunch.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: recurring wheezing and shortness of breath. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €30.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: The baton stayed behind
decisions.situation: You and Lorenzo complete a spectacular relay changeover. Both of you are sprinting. The baton is still on the ground beside Leonardo.

choices.label: Try again, this time with the baton
Claim Lorenzo was meant to collect it

result.title: Equipment included
result.body: You slow down and practise the handover. Carrying the actual baton makes your teamwork much more convincing.

journal.text: I practised a failed relay handover with Lorenzo.

decisions.title: A nose for music
decisions.situation: Lorenzo has learned to play the recorder with their nose. They ask you to accompany their debut. The first note makes everyone check for a trapped bird.

choices.label: Drum on the desk and let them have their moment
Offer to be the audience from further away
Announce that you can play an imaginary one

result.title: A very short tour
result.body: You find a beat that nearly matches the squeaks. Lorenzo attempts an encore, sneezes, and announces an interval.

journal.text: I accompanied Lorenzo’s nose-recorder debut by drumming on a desk.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Alice one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Agree on one round each, then stop

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Alice seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Alice I would.

decisions.title: Immortal words, wrong person
decisions.situation: The yearbook proof puts Lorenzo’s quote under your photo: “I peaked at nine.” Alice needs corrections today. You are not sure you want to ask what happened at nine.

choices.label: Return the quote to its rightful owner
Approve it as your mysterious backstory

result.title: A corrected confession
result.body: Alice fixes the names. Lorenzo explains that they won a particularly good sack race.

journal.text: I corrected swapped yearbook quotations.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Alice plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Alice.

journal.text: I listened to Alice’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: Your stand-in has a meeting
decisions.situation: To dodge chores, you left a dummy in your dressing gown at your desk. Alice is now giving it a serious talk about responsibility. The dummy is handling it well.

choices.label: Step out and take over the discussion
Leave a second dummy to play Alice
Stay hidden and let the dummy handle it

result.title: A noticeable improvement in posture
result.body: Alice says the dummy already agreed to take the rubbish out. You do it while the dummy remains at the desk, apparently thinking about its future.

journal.text: I replaced a dummy during Alice’s lecture and did the chore it had agreed to.

decisions.title: The accidental millionaire
decisions.situation: At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Admit your wealth has been exaggerated
Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

result.title: A donkey-sized misunderstanding
result.body: You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.
I was born on 29 February 2024 in Milan, Italy.
My name is Leonardo Ricci. I’m a girl.
My mother is Alice Ricci, 24. She works as a plumber.
At home, it’s just my mother and me. My mother asked whether I came with instructions. She was handed another form.
I made faces at my reflection and laughed when it copied me.
I drew a purple person on the wall. It was not a commissioned piece.
I showed Alice the ice cube I had hidden in my sock.
I developed symptoms: a runny nose, sore throat and tiredness.
My symptoms resolved.
I tried magic during a haircut. It did not affect the comb.
I gave Alice a museum tour while a slug escaped from my pocket collection.
I started at Milan Primary School.
Leonardo Ricci became my class teacher at Milan Primary School.
I got to know Lorenzo, Sofia, Giulia in my class at Milan Primary School.
I backed Lorenzo when someone kept mocking their name.
My primary school-year report recorded grades of 38%. I completed twelve attended months at Milan Primary School.
